text:
Marta: heads-up — after enabling ingress deflate on the canary cluster at 18:02 we saw host CPU jump and streaming latency regressions on short-chat loads :eyes:
Chris: saw the same in tracing, p50 up ~12ms for 256-512 token streams. Looks tied to more frequent 1-2KB frames being emitted after compression.
Sam: throwing logs here from the canary gateway:
```
2026-03-17T18:03:11Z ingress-gw[pid=7421] INFO wrote frame size=1500 compressed=420 time_us=2100
2026-03-17T18:03:11Z ingress-gw[pid=7421] INFO wrote frame size=600 compressed=210 time_us=1900
2026-03-17T18:03:12Z backend-proxy[pid=8009] WARN grpc_writev: 8 iovecs, syscall=writev duration_us=1200
```
Jules: interesting — writev syscalls increased and each syscall cost is amplified by extra CPU for zlib inflate/deflate on the hot path. That plus smaller frames is hurting batching.
Nikhil: that also explains kernel-selection thrash we saw in the server: model kernel lookup optimized for average length, but more micro-requests change the sequence distribution; runtime falls back to safer kernels more often.
Marta: repro steps I used: `wrk -t4 -c32 --latency -d30s` with the compressed header toggled. Repro still cheaper in network but host-side compute > network savings for short requests.
Chris: quick profiling:
```
# perf top sample
25.2%  libz.so       deflate_internal
18.6%  runtime        parse_incoming_stream
9.3%   kernel_selector choose_kernel_by_seq
6.7%   grpc           writev_wrapper
```
Sam: KV cache note — with smaller compressed chunks, requests arrive fragmented differently, kv cache lookup frequency increases due to prefix mismatches, causing more KV cache eviction churn on some hot shards. Not huge but measurable on p95.
Jules: immediate mitigations: 1) back out compression for short sessions (client hint), 2) coalesce frames at gateway to target >=1.2KB before compress, 3) increase batcher timeout by 1-2ms to allow micro-requests to join existing batch.
Marta: tried coalesce + larger target size on canary. CPU down ~18% and p50 restored, p95 still a bit high due to kv thrash.
Nikhil: long-term: kernel selector should be aware of the framing distribution; if many tiny frames, bias toward low-init-cost kernels. Also batching heuristics can use an ingress-provided "coalesced" flag to be more aggressive.
Chris: action items: @Jules try coalesce threshold tweak in canary for another 4hr run; @Sam run kv shard heatmap during the test; @Nikhil can you prototype kernel-selection flag that prefers fast-path kernels when avg-seq-length < 64 and frame_count>8?
Sam: will dump heatmap + eviction counts and post results.
Jules: starting canary tweak now — toggling target_coalesce_bytes=1200 and batch_delay_ms=2, will post metrics. :hammer:
ingress-bot: deploy canary completed 2409876555 (version=ingress-3.7.1-deflate-experiment)
Marta: thanks all, keeping this thread for quick notes. If we need a deeper postmortem we can spin up a short doc but for now prefer incremental experiments. :thumbsup:
